messages.author: a2c316298c1ee632
messages.subject: shiny server upgrade problem
parts:
I've upgraded my shiny server installation so that I can host .Rmd files. The installation was only 4 months old, I'm not sure what version number. 

Now, I can see my .Rmd files, but I can't see my shiny apps or even the sample-apps/hello app. I'm running the default version of /etc/shiny-server/shiny-server.conf.

When I try to browse to an app page, it says "Not Found"

Any ideas?

Thanks

Cory

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: shiny server upgrade problem
parts:
Is it possible that the apps you're trying to access are in a subdirectory of a folder that contains .Rmd files? For example:

/srv/shiny-server/hello.Rmd
/srv/shiny-server/app1/

If so, it's because when an .Rmd file is present in a directory, Shiny Server considers that directory to be a Shiny app--it won't serve any apps that are contained therein. Sorry, this is really confusing now that I look at it.

If this isn't the case with your setup, please let us know.

messages.author: bff9e4feca8b059f
messages.subject: Re: shiny server upgrade problem
parts:
I have a related issue: I have a directory tree of shiny-runtime .Rmd files, and because there's no auto-indexing with directory URLs, there's and index.Rmd in each directory that auto-builds a page of links for that directory (and subdirs). However, this only works for the top level directory, all other subdirectories fail to completely load, because the relative URLs for, e.g. "shared/shiny.css" cannot be found.  In other words:

server.name/top/shared/shiny.css -- exists
server.name/top/sub/shared/shiny.css -- not found

even though server.name/top/sub/foo.Rmd does seem to trigger the shiny runtime process.

Any config I can do to serve these URLs (or set base href to the top/ directory)?

thanks,
-Aaron
